I considered raising it, since this text becomes the rule future agents apply, and settled on opus because the PR gets a seat review *and* a human merge before it can bind anyone.

Merge-order risk is therefore nil, but if any of them lands first, merge `main` before opening this PR.

## ⛔ Governed surface — landing rule, stated up front

`AGENTS.md` and `skills/**` are governed. This PR gets drafted, pushed, and reviewed by me, then **left visibly waiting for the maintainer to merge by hand**. I will not flip it ready for auto-merge, will not enqueue it, and will not merge it. "Reviewed + green" is not an exception. Open it as a draft and leave it there.

## The ruling to implement (settled; do not re-litigate)

Option A of three, chosen by the maintainer: amend the docs to carve out data-driven author-declared colour, keeping the ban on component-authored static colour. Options B (case-by-case exceptions) and C (ESLint-enforced flat ban) were explicitly **not** chosen — in particular, **do not add or propose a lint rule**, and do not audit the 254 existing `style={{` sites.

## What makes this card easy to get wrong

The failure mode is writing a carve-out so loose it reads as "inline styles are fine now". The boundary has to be sharp enough to decide the *next* case without a human:

- the permitted shape is **author-declared, data-driven colour published as CSS custom properties consumed by static utilities** — the worked reference is `getBadgeHexAppearance` / `getDotHexAppearance` in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` (PR #5184, landing now);
- the hazard the original rule exists to prevent should be **named**: an inline style that hard-codes a colour so dark mode renders identically. Write that down, because it is the property that actually distinguishes the two cases — not the presence of the word `style`;
- carry the **rationale**, not just the rule: semantic tokens exist so theming and dark mode work automatically. A pattern preserving that satisfies the rule; one defeating it does not.

## Verify before you write

The evidence in the card body was measured by me on `origin/main` and is a clue, not a specification — re-derive it. In particular re-check the `254` count and the three existing author-colour paths (`plugin-gantt` bars, `conditionalFormatting`, Studio's option swatch) before citing any number in the docs. **Prefer not to cite a raw count in the doc text at all** — a number in prose rots the moment someone adds a call site, and this repo already has cards open about exactly that failure mode. Describe the shape, not the census.

Read the current text of both files first: if §2 or `styling.md` already carries a partial exception, amend it in place rather than appending a second, competing paragraph.

## Gates

Derive from your actual diff. A docs-only change here implicates at least `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, and the changeset gates. **That list is a clue, not a spec.** Note `Skill Guide Path Check` specifically — you are editing under `skills/`, so it is live for this diff.

Changeset: docs-only. This repo has **no** `skip-changeset` label and one must **never** be minted; if no released package changes, an empty-frontmatter changeset is the sanctioned declaration.

## Premise-first

If the current text already says something equivalent, or the ruling turns out not to fit the file structure, report `premise_still_valid: false` with evidence rather than forcing an edit.

## Deliver

**Draft** PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5185`, and leave it draft. Push the branch early.

Return the structured JSON report AND post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`.

**ACCEPT — and held for a human merge, permanently.** PR #5188 (`repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`, reviewer of record).

**Landing path: governed surface, terminal three-piece.** `AGENTS.md` and `skills/**` are agent-instruction files that only the maintainer may merge. PR #5188 stays **draft**; I have not flipped it ready, not enabled auto-merge, not enqueued it, and will not. Listed under *awaiting a human merge* in my round report. Green and reviewed is not an exception — the human merge **is** the review record for this surface.

**CI: 19 checks, all terminal — 17 success, 2 skipped, zero failures.** (19 rather than 21 because a docs-only diff doesn't run Bundle Analysis or Live E2E.) `Skill Guide Path Check` is green and is genuinely live for this diff, which matters: it's the gate that would catch a broken path reference in a `skills/` guide.

**Scope: exactly the declared surface** — `AGENTS.md`, `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md`, and an empty-frontmatter changeset (the sanctioned docs-only declaration; no `skip-changeset` label minted, correctly). No lint rule added or proposed, no existing `style={{}}` site audited, `packages/fields` untouched. Options B and C stayed shut.

**The deviation is the best thing in this PR.** The dispatch named two files; the dev amended four sections plus the top blockquote, and was right to. Two of them were live contradictions that a minimal edit would have left in place:

- *"Rule: Dark Mode with Semantic Tokens"* says **"DO NOT manually add `dark:` variants"** — which is exactly backwards for the sanctioned carrier, where an explicit `dark:` variant is what *keeps* dark mode real. Left alone, the guide would have banned the pattern it had just permitted, two screens apart.
- *"Rule: Use Semantic Color Tokens"* banned `bg-[#3b82f6]` as **"Arbitrary value"** — but the sanctioned carrier `bg-[color:var(--os-badge-bg)]` **is** an arbitrary value. Sharpening the ban to the colour *literal* rather than the syntax is the correct fix and is the difference between a rule that decides cases and one that contradicts itself.

That is precisely the "two rules in one document that disagree is worse than the flat rule you are fixing" hazard, found and closed without being told which sections.

**The text is decidable, which was the whole point.** It names the hazard in *both* files — an inline style that hard-codes a colour such that dark mode renders identically — and says outright that this, not the presence of the word `style`, is the property that decides a case. It carries the rationale as a *test* ("Read that rationale as the test. It decides cases this page does not list"), and it scopes hard: colour only, author-declared only, with runtime **geometry** explicitly named as a separate question this carve-out does not answer. That last sentence is what stops the next reader widening this into "inline styles are fine now".

**Two measurement notes I'm recording because they correct me:**

1. **My census was already stale when I wrote it.** I measured 254 `style={{` under `packages/*/src`; the dev re-derived **260** the same day. Neither number is in the doc — which is exactly why I asked for the shape rather than a count, and the same-day drift is the argument, not a hypothetical.
2. **The carve-out does not retroactively bless the three paths I cited to the maintainer.** Re-measured, all three — `plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx:3637`, `ruleToStyle` in `core/src/evaluator/listConditional.ts:381`, `app-shell/.../SchemaForm.tsx:1701` — use the **direct** form (`style={{ backgroundColor: … }}`), which the new rule forbids. The doc correctly cites them as the practice that made the flat rule untrue, **not** as conforming examples. So after this lands they are non-conforming-but-unenforced, exactly as they were before. Auditing them was explicitly out of scope here; whether they should be migrated to the carrier pattern is a real follow-up question and I am flagging it rather than filing unilaterally, since it is capability-shaped work across three packages.

**Worked reference now resolves.** It was drafted while PR #5184 was still open, so the dev read the symbols from that PR's head and stated the pattern in full inline so the rule stands alone. #5184 has since merged (`a09bc33ff`), and I confirmed on `main` that `getBadgeHexAppearance` (:1409), `getDotHexAppearance` (:1427) and the exact quoted carrier string (:1393) are all live.
